entries.title: I Kings 1:1
segments: If life is spared, age and infirmities will come, and no means or efforts of men can save any one from death.  All should therefore make it their great object so to live that death shall be gain.

entries.title: I Kings 1:6
segments: Bare him after; he was next in age to Absalom, whose mother's name was Maacah.
Over-indulgent parents are often cursed with rebellious children; and inordinate desires for political distinctions have involved multitudes in ruin.

entries.title: I Kings 1:8
segments: Shimei; supposed to have been Shimei the son of Elah, afterwards one of Solomon's officers.

entries.title: I Kings 1:9
segments:
En-rogel; a fountain on the south-east of Jerusalem, in the valley of Kedron. 
 
Feastings and carousals have strong attractions for the thoughtless, and are often used to draw them into dissipation and crime.

entries.title: I Kings 1:12
segments: Save thine own life, and the life of thy son; had Adonijah succeeded, it would have been his policy to put Solomon, and probably his mother also, to death; as the people knew that David intended that he should be his successor, and there would have been a strong party in his favor.
All wise and proper means should be used to prevent the success of evil projects, and aid those which will honor God and benefit men.

entries.title: I Kings 1:21
segments:
I and my son Solomon shall be counted offenders; we shall be regarded and treated as persons deserving to die. 
 
Parents should do what is practicable to prevent evils from coming on their families after their death, and to secure for them permanent blessings.

entries.title: I Kings 1:27
segments: Good rulers, who have secured general confidence, may by their dying advice greatly promote the welfare of their people.

entries.title: I Kings 1:32
segments: What is essential for the public good should not be postponed, lest the opportunity of doing it be lost; but should be undertaken with promptness, and prosecuted with energy till it is accomplished.

entries.title: I Kings 1:33
segments: Gihon; a fountain on the west side of Jerusalem.

entries.title: I Kings 1:37
segments: When God is duly acknowledged as the author of all good, men may reasonably expect that their blessings will be increased.

entries.title: I Kings 1:49
segments: The most sanguine projects of the wicked are destined to disappointment; and from the heights of expectation they may suddenly be thrown into the depths of despair.

entries.title: I Kings 1:50
segments: Horns of the altar; as a sacred place, where it was not customary to put criminals to death.  The wilful murderer was to be taken from the altar before he was slain.

entries.title: I Kings 1:52
segments: Will show himself a worthy man--if wickedness shall be found in him; Solomon will pass by for the present Adonijah's offence, and put him upon his good behavior.
